events.label: Holmes makes a statement about life being stranger than fiction

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: life is infinitely stranger than anything which the mind of man could invent.

events.label: Holmes makes a statement about commonplaces of existence not being dared to be conceived

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: We would not dare to conceive the things which are really mere commonplaces of existence.

events.label: Holmes makes a statement about flying out a window and peeping into city events

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: If we could fly out of that window hand in hand, hover over this great city, gently remove the roofs, and peep in at the queer things which are going on, the strange coincidences, the plannings, the cross-purposes, the wonderful chains of events, working through generations, and leading to the most outré results, it would make all fiction with its conventionalities and foreseen conclusions most stale and unprofitable.

events.label: Watson answers that he is not convinced

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: And yet I am not convinced of it

events.label: Holmes makes a statement about cases in papers being bald and vulgar

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: The cases which come to light in the papers are, as a rule, bald enough, and vulgar enough.

events.label: Watson makes a statement about police reports realism and their lack of fascination or artistry

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: We have in our police reports realism pushed to its extreme limits, and yet the result is, it must be confessed, neither fascinating nor artistic.

events.label: Holmes remarks that selection and discretion are needed for realistic effect

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: A certain selection and discretion must be used in producing a realistic effect,

events.label: Holmes makes a statement about police reports focusing on magistrates' platitudes rather than vital details

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: This is wanting in the police report, where more stress is laid, perhaps, upon the platitudes of the magistrate than upon the details, which to an observer contain the vital essence of the whole matter.

events.label: Holmes makes a statement that nothing is so unnatural as the commonplace

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Depend upon it, there is nothing so unnatural as the commonplace.

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: I can quite understand your thinking so.

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: Of course, in your position of unofficial adviser and helper to everybody who is absolutely puzzled, throughout three continents, you are brought in contact with all that is strange and bizarre.

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: But here—let us put it to a practical test.

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: Here is the first heading upon which I come.

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: A husband’s cruelty to his wife.

events.label: Watson makes a statement about familiarity and describes elements associated with the heading

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: There is half a column of print, but I know without reading it that it is all perfectly familiar to me. There is, of course, the other woman, the drink, the push, the blow, the bruise, the sympathetic sister or landlady. The crudest of writers could invent nothing more crude.

communicates.content: Indeed, your example is an unfortunate one for your argument

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: This is the Dundas separation case, and, as it happens, I was engaged in clearing up some small points in connection with it.

events.label: Holmes states details that differ from Watson's example

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: The husband was a teetotaler, there was no other woman, and the conduct complained of was that he had drifted into the habit of winding up every meal by taking out his false teeth and hurling them at his wife, which, you will allow, is not an action likely to occur to the imagination of the average story-teller.

events.label: Holmes tells Watson to take a pinch of snuff and acknowledge he has scored over him

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Take a pinch of snuff, Doctor, and acknowledge that I have scored over you in your example.

communicates.content: He would not go to the police, and he would not go to you, and so at last, as he would do nothing and kept on saying that there was no harm done, it made me mad, and I just on with my things and came right away to you.

communicates.speaker: miss_mary_sutherland

communicates.content: They got £4700 for the goodwill and interest, which wasn’t near as much as father could have got if he had been alive.

communicates.speaker: miss_mary_sutherland
communicates.content: I could do with much less than that, Mr. Holmes, but you understand that as long as I live at home I don’t wish to be a burden to them, and so they have the use of the money just while I am staying with them. Of course, that is only just for the time. Mr. Windibank draws my interest every quarter and pays it over to mother, and I find that I can do pretty well with what I earn at typewriting.

clues.significance: Holmes received a slip and four letters from Hosmer Angel that Irene Adler placed into the case materials for the Hosmer Angel investigation.
Holmes uses a typewritten letter to establish the timing for the six o’clock appointment in connection with the ongoing matters involving Miss Mary Sutherland.

Holmes pointed to four typewritten letters that showed slurring over of the 'e' and a tailless 'r', along with fourteen other consistent characteristics, matching a specific typewriter pattern using his magnifying lens.

Holmes identified the man by noting his signature was typed in a way that implied familiarity of his handwriting to Miss Sutherland and inferred that this typing indicated the smallest sample would be recognizable.
